standard_prerequisites.name: Finite type algebras over a quasi-excellent ring are quasi-excellent
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the claim to quasi-excellent domains.

standard_prerequisites.name: The criterion for the universally Japanese property, and its characterisation through J-2 and the local case

standard_prerequisites.name: The completion of a quasi-excellent local ring is reduced, i.e. the ring is analytically unramified, and analytic unramifiedness implies the universal Japanese property

core_obligations: Reduce to showing that a quasi-excellent domain is universally Japanese (proof lines 13469-13471).
Use the characterisation of that property and the J-2 property to pass to quasi-excellent local domains (proof lines 13472-13474).
Show the completion is reduced via regularity of the completion map, i.e. that the ring is analytically unramified (proof lines 13475-13479).
Conclude the universal Japanese property from the standard criterion (proof lines 13480-13482).
proof_roadmap: Reduction to the local case (proof lines 13472-13474).
Analytic unramifiedness and the final criterion (proof lines 13475-13482).
difficulty_reason: The lemma deduces the Nagata property from quasi-excellence. The proof uses that finite type algebras over a quasi-excellent ring are quasi-excellent to reduce to showing that a quasi-excellent domain is universally Japanese, then reduces further, using the characterisation of that property together with the J-2 property of quasi-excellent rings, to the case of a quasi-excellent local domain. There the regularity of the completion map makes the completion reduced, which says exactly that the ring is analytically unramified, and the standard criterion then gives the universal Japanese property.
